purpose: Close the fixed-global-H2 semantic blocker by indexing every presentation and evaluation by the actual group H2(X) of its manifold.

implementation.name: presentation_reindexing
implementation.result: A presentation over H2 can be reindexed along any additive equivalence H2 ~= H2'. The evaluator is proved unchanged after the corresponding marking transport.

implementation.name: dependent_movie_descent
implementation.result: Finite movies are explicit inductive objects. Their marking transport is recursively composed, and evaluation invariance is proved by induction from the eight local move theorems.

implementation.name: public_dependent_interface
implementation.result: The public input is the dependent pair (X, alpha) with alpha in H2(X). The diffeomorphism theorem compares alpha with the induced H2 map.

implementation.name: stale_fixed_h2_bridge
implementation.result: REMOVED. It was unimported, duplicated obsolete fixed-H2 semantics, and was not part of the successful build.

topology_boundary.non_content: These axioms do not mention a premodular category, tensor automorphism, evaluator, or scalar equality.

checks.name: proof_hole_scan
checks.scope: All changed and newly added Lean sources

established: There is no global auxiliary H2 in the public invariant route.
For every manifold X, the internal presentation is indexed by H2(X).
Evaluation is invariant under reindexing by an additive equivalence.
Evaluation is invariant along explicit finite movies by induction on the eight local move theorems.
The public premodular TwistedYetter value is invariant under oriented diffeomorphism with alpha transported by the induced H2 map.
The modular theorem is a specialization of the premodular theorem.
not_established: Equality with the original Crane-Yetter state-sum definition.
Re-certification of legacy modular numerical artifacts under the corrected role-aware evaluator.
A single monolithic structure-equivalence theorem matching every field of every independent semantic specification file to the implementation.
